IS : 11750 . 1986 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

BRUSH FITCH, FLAT, WITH 

LONG HANDLE 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 30 April 1986, after the draft finalized by the Brushware Sectional 
Conimittee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 

0.2 Brushes, fiat fitch with long handle are used for studio work by art 
designers and sign painters. In this type of brushes, the filling materials 
being short in protrusion give greater springiness and elasticity to the 
brush. And by virtue of being flat at the tips, this type of brushes arc 
found more suitable for broad letter writing and figure painting jobs than 
the round type of artists' or lettering brushes. 

0.3 Fitch brushes with bristles as filling material are suitable for oil 
painting, specially upon canvas or rough surface. Fitch brushes with mon- 
goose hair as filling material are used for working with water colours and 
upon smooth or delicate ground. 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final values, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified values 
in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1,1 This standard prescribes jJie requirements, methods of test and 
sampling for brushes fitch, flat with long handle. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, definitions given in IS: 5060-1969t, 
IS : 707-1960t, and the one given below shall apply. 

•RulcJ for rounding off numerical values ( rtvistd. ) 

fGlotsary of terms used in brushware industry. 

^Glossary of terms applicable to timber technology and utilization ( stetnd revititn ). 



IS : 11750 - 1986 

2.1.1 Approved Tender Sample — The sample accepted by the indentor 
or inspection authority as basis of supply. When a sample is tested and 
approved by the purchaser or an inspection authority, the results of such 
tests as will permit the supplier to meet the limits imposed by the specifi- 
cation for deliveries shall be made available to the supplier. 

3. GRADES 

3.1 Brushes fitch shall be of the folJowirg two grades, depending on the 
nature of the filling material. 

a) GRADE 1 — with white bristles, and 

b) GRADE 2 — with mongoose hair. 

4. SIZES 

4.1 Each grade of brushes filch shall have 14 sizes as given in Table 1. 

5. REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Materials — The brushes shall be manufactured from the following 
material. 

5.1.1 Filling Materials 

5.1.1.1 For grade I — Selected, soft or stifT/semi-stiff white bristles of 
natural, uniform colour and properly straightened. 

5.1.1.2 i''or ^ra^e 2 — Selected mongoose hair of natural colour and 
free from adulterants, 

5.1.1.3 As regards colour, lustre, stiffness, flexibility and fineness of 
the filling materials, these shall match those used jn the approved tender 
sample. 

5.1.2 Timber — Any of the timber species listed in Appendix A shall be 
used in the manufacture of handles of the brushes. 

5.1.2.1 The timber shall be reasonably straight-grained and well 
seasoned to a moisture content not exceeding IS percent when tested by 
the moisture meter or in case of dispute by the over- dry method given in 
Appendix B. 

5.1.2.2 The timber shall be free from brashness, any kind of biological 
or non-biological deterioration, insect attack, centre-heart ( pith ), knots 
except live pin knots, cracks, warp and any other defect which may reduce 
the life of the brush or affect its utility.

5.1.3 Ferrule — The ferrule shall be flat at the top and round at the 
bottom. The ferrule shall be seamless, rickel-platcd brass and in case of 
tin plate it shall be lapped and soldered. Ferrule shall be made of 0'27 to 
0*31 mm thick nickel-plated brass sheet or tin plate. 

5.1.4 Cement — Any cement suitable for firm anchorage of the filling 
material inside the ferrule shall be used. The anchorage shall satisfy the 
pull test prescribed in 6.1. 

5.1,4.1 In no case the setting cement shall appear out of the ferrule. 

5.2 Dimensioni «nd Tolerancei 

5.2.1 Dimensions 

5.2.1,1 Brushes, flat litch shall conform to the dimensions given in 
Table J. 

5.2.2 Tolerances — The tolerance on the linear dimensions shall be as 
follows : 



Nominal Dimension 


Tolerance 


mm 


mm 


Up to 15 


±10 


Over 15 but below 40 


±2-0 


40 and above 


±30 



Tolerance for the length of filling material out of the ferrule shall 

bet I 

5.2.3 The solid dressing of the filling materials shall conform to those 
used in the approved tender sample, 

5.3 Manufacture 

5.3.1 Brushes, flat fitch shall correspond to the shape and design as 
shown in Fig. 1 . 

5.3.2 Working Edge — The tip of the brushes shall be flat, thin and of 
even edge. 

5.3.3 The ferrule shall be fully filled with the filling material and there 
shall be no gap at the mouth of the ferrule. This shall be ascertained by 
pressing the filling material at the mouth of the ferrule. 

5.4 Workmanship and Finish 

5.4.1 The ferrule shall be free from sharp edges. 

5.4.2 The bandies shall be neatly turned or shaped to conform to the 
design shown in Fig. 1. The handles shall be finished smooth, suitably 
varnished or lacquered, clear or coloured as agreed to between the supplier 
and the purchaser. 



18:11750-1986 





5 



I 



£ 



o 



15:11750-1986 

5.4 J The handles shall be tight-fitted by clinching at the round-end of 
the ferrule. 

5.4.4 In general workmanship and finish, the brushes shall match the 
approved tender sample. 

6. PRESERVATION 

6.1 The filling material of the brushes shall be liberally dusted before 
packing, with a mixture of 5 parts ( by mass ) of DDT dusting powder ( see 
IS : 564.I975* ) and 95 parts (by mass) of French chalk {see IS: 
380-1 978t). Ahernatively, naphthalene balls may be used in the packing 
box for the brushes. 

7. PACKING AND MARKING 

7.1 Packing — The brushes shall be packed as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. 

7.2 Marking — Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier, each brush shall be legibly and indelibly marked or stamped with 
the manufacturer's name or recognized trade-mark, if any, the year of 
manufacture, the grade and size denomination and the warranty of the 
filling material of the brush. 

7.2.1 The brush may also be marked with the IS[ Certification Mark. 

NoTB — The use or the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations 
made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys 
the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that 
standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is 
devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are 
also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. 
Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or processors may be obtained from the Indian 
Sandards Institution. 

8. TENDER SAMPLES AND SAMPLING 

t 

8.1 Tender Samples — The supplier shall submit four identical tender 
samples of brushes of each denomination and grade for approval. 

8.1.1 The indentor or inspection authority shall retain one of the four 
approved tender samples against each item, till the completion of order. 

8.2 Sampling — The method of drawing representative samples of the 
brushes and the criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in 
Appendix C.

9. TEST METHODS 



9.1 Pull Test — The cement shall not fail when a small bunch of the filling 
nuterial is subjected to a straight pull with thumb-and-iinger grip. 

9.2 Performance Tei t — The tuft end of the brush shall be dipped in water 
and withdrawn and then given a slight jerk. The tuft shall assume the 
shape as shown in Fig. 1 .

APPENDIX B 

{Clatdse 5.1.24) 

DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT FOR 
TIMBER USED IN BRUSHES, FLAT FITCH 

B-l. TEST SPECIMEN 

B-1<1 The entire block used in flat fitch brushes may form the test 
specimen for determinatioa of moisture content or a coupon cut from the 
test specimen may, as well» be used for moisture content determination. 
When for any reason additional determination of moisture content is 
required, separate samples shall be prepared from the sample material as 
is used in preparing the test specimens. Smaller specimens may be used 
when deetned necessary. The test shall be carried out immediately after 
cutting the specimen. 



10 



15:11750-1986 

B-2. PROCEDURE 

B-2.1 Weigh accurately each test specimen. This specimen shall then be 
dried in a ventilated oven at a temperature of 105 ± 2*C until the mass 
becomes constant between two successive weighings made at an interval 
of not less than one hour. 

B-3. CALCULATION 

B-3.1 The moisture content, expressed as a percentage of the oven-dry 
mass is given by the formula : 

Moisture content, percent by mass = — ^ X lOO 

where 

A/i «" initial mass in g of test specimen, and 
Afo « oven-dry mass in g of the test specimen. 

APPENDIX C 

( Ciause 8.2 ) 

SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY FOR 
BRUSHES FLAT FITCH 

C-1. SAMPLING 

C-1.1 Lot — In any consignment, all the brushes of the same size and 
type shall be divided into groups of 500 brushes or less and each such 
group shall constitute a lot. Care shall be taken to ensure that brushes 
included in a lot do not differ in construction, as far as possible. 

C-1. 1.1 The conformity of the brushes in a lot to the requirements of 
this specification shall be ascertained for each lot separately. The number 
of brushes to be selected for ihis purpose shall be in accordance with col 1 
and 2 of Table 2. 

C-1.1.2 The brushes shall be selected at random. To ensure random- 
ness of selection, one of the following procedures is recommended for 
use : 

a) If all the brushes in a lot are packed in one box, then starting 

from any brush, count them in any suitable order as 1, 2, , 

up to r and so on, where ris the integral part of N}n ( N and n 
being the lot size and sample size respectively). Every rth brush 
thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample. 

U 



IS: 11750 -1986 

b) If the brushes in a lot are packed in more than one box, approxi- 
mately equal number of brushes shall be picked at random from 
as many boxes as possible so as to obtain the required number of 
brushes as specified in Table 2.
